KKA0231-TCBM1.lead: An oval loaf tin for rounded milk breads, brioche and small tea cakes.
p: The Kitchenary Kart Oval Shaped Teflon Coated Bread Mould bakes a loaf with rounded ends in place of square corners. At 20 cm long it takes one small bake: a braided sweet bread, a brioche, or a row of rolled dough coils that rise together into a pull-apart bread.

The black non-stick coating lets the crust come away cleanly, and the tin also holds cake batter for an oval tea cake. Home bakers and cafés selling single loaves or gift breads get a rounded shape that looks neat on a display shelf.

Coating: Matte black Teflon non-stick lining.
KKA0231-TCBM1.suit: Milk bread, brioche, braided sweet loaves, pull-apart rolls and small oval tea cakes.
KKA0231-TCBM1.care: Brush a thin layer of butter or oil inside before filling. Wash by hand with a soft sponge and mild soap, keep knives and steel scrubbers off the coating, and dry fully before storing.

Folded corners keep the walls square, so slices stay the same shape from one end to the other. Bakeries use it for multigrain and whole-wheat bread, while cafés bake their own loaves for grilled sandwiches.

KKA0232-TCBM2.suit: Toast and brown bread, multigrain loaves, banana loaf and pound cake.
KKA0232-TCBM2.care: Let the tin cool before washing. Use a soft cloth or sponge with a little detergent, skip metal spatulas and wire scrubbers that scratch the gold coating, and towel-dry before stacking.

Its shallow depth gives a lower loaf that slices neatly onto tea plates. The dark coating and rounded corners let the cake turn out in one piece.

Once firm, bend the tray and press each cavity from underneath to pop the domes out whole. Chocolatiers fill them with ganache or chopped nuts, and sweet shops pack them into festive gift boxes.

Sweet shops use it to speed up gujiya and karanji before Holi and Diwali, and cloud kitchens turn out half-moon momos and empanadas with it. The two halves join at a riveted hinge, and the bare steel wipes clean between batches.
